subject: Azure co-sell: claims alignment & support window matrix for marketplace listing
messages:
From: Melissa Chang <melissa.chang@amazon.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Azure listing: creative claims + support window requirements

Hi Rachel / Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Quick follow-up from the AWS listing intake team: before we can approve co-sell enablement for the Azure SKU on the marketplace, we need a final set of marketing claim strings and a mapping of customer support coverage (support hours / escalation path) that will appear on the listing. Key asks:

- One-line product description (<= 140 chars)
- Up to three marketing claims (no superlatives that imply exclusivity: avoid "best", "only", "guaranteed")
- Support hours matrix (local time zones + SLA for dedicated vs hosted deployments)
- Any required compliance call-outs (SOC 2, encryption-at-rest)

Attached is the most recent AWS_Listing_Guidelines_2027.pdf — see section 3.4 on allowed claims and the support disclosure template. Can you send back a proposed copy and a small spreadsheet mapping support tiers by region?

AWS Legal is looped to flag anything that needs softer phrasing. Deadline to hit the next co-sell batch is March 12 so ideally we have a reviewed draft by March 8.

Thanks,
Melissa
Melissa Chang | GTM Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
Attachments: AWS_Listing_Guidelines_2027.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Melissa Chang <melissa.chang@amazon.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure listing: creative claims + support window requirements

Melissa — thanks for the checklist and the deadline. Looping in Karthik and Laura to own legal phrasing and support coverage respectively.

We can deliver the one-line and three claims + a support-hours matrix. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we finalize:

1) For "support hours" the marketplace asks for timezone-specific windows. Do we need to provide 24/7 coverage for US customers to qualify for co-sell, or is business-hours with on-call escalation acceptable?
2) Are we expected to call out Dedicated vs Hosted differences on the public listing or only in the private co-sell enablement materials?

Plan: I’ll draft proposed claim language and a CSV of support windows by EMEA/APAC/US for Laura to verify. Karthik — if you can run a quick pass on allowed claim phrasing (especially any required qualifiers), that would be great.

Target: internal sign-off by EOD March 7 so we can send to AWS Legal on March 8.

—
Rachel Kim
Sr. Partner GTM | Redwood Inference
——
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Melissa Chang <melissa.chang@amazon.com>, AWS Marketplace Legal <marketplace-legal@amazonaws.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure listing: creative claims + support window requirements

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed section 3.4 and drafted safer variants for the marketing claims. High-level guidance: avoid absolute or comparative adjectives, and where we reference performance or cost savings, qualify with a timeframe or typical workload. Examples below (suggested final copy in quotes):

- One-line product description (<=140 chars): "Redwood Inference — predictable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."

- Claim 1: "Consistent inference performance across cloud and on-prem deployments with predictable latency SLOs."
- Claim 2: "Tools for cost-aware serving: intelligent batching, caching, and quantization recommendations."
- Claim 3: "Enterprise controls for data isolation, audit logs, and key management integrations."

Notes:
- For any metric-like claim (e.g., "<50 ms tail latency"), we need an explicit benchmark URL or a qualifying phrase such as "typical" or "in many workloads."
- If AWS Legal requests softer language, we can switch to "helps reduce inference latency" vs "reduces latency."

I also recommend we include a brief compliance line: "SOC 2 Type II compliant; encryption at rest and in transit." That aligns with the guideline examples.

Happy to iterate — if anyone prefers, I can produce a tracked-change version for Legal.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head, General Counsel (advisory) — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Melissa Chang <melissa.chang@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Azure listing: creative claims + support window requirements

Team — attaching a support-hours matrix (see below summary) and how we propose to present differences between Hosted vs Dedicated on the marketplace listing. Attachment: support-hours-matrix.csv

Summary (proposed public listing disclosure):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Standard support: Mon–Fri 6am–6pm PT (business hours). Critical incidents: 24/7 on-call escalation with response target 1 hour for P1.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Standard support: Mon–Fri 6am–6pm PT. Dedicated customers can opt into premium 24/7 coverage for an additional contract addendum; response targets in the SLA appendix.

We suggest framing the public listing with the business-hours baseline and adding a short sentence: "24/7 critical-incident escalation available for production customers; see support terms in contract." That keeps the listing truthful without promising always-on coverage by default.

Marissa — can you confirm whether this messaging aligns with co-sell enablement docs you use in partner playbooks?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Strategic Partnerships — Redwood Inference
Attachment: support-hours-matrix.csv (text/csv)

• "Tools for cost-aware serving, including intelligent batching, caching, and quantization recommendations."
• "Enterprise controls for data isolation, audit logs, and key management integrations."

• Dedicated: Mon–Fri 6am–6pm PT; premium 24/7 support available via contract.

Attachments: redwood-final-claims-copy.txt, support-hours-matrix.csv

Best,
Rachel Kim
